method: python training/evaluate_beyond_accuracy.py --data-dir ml-32m Same viewers and same 3 random likes as the benchmark (first 1-in-5 slice, the 3,000 test viewers, seed 5), so these sit next to the accuracy numbers. For each viewer, each model's top 10 (movies they already liked removed): - Catalog coverage: share of the benchmark's movies that appear in at least one viewer's top 10. - Popularity of picks: average fan percentile of the top 10 (0 = fewest MovieLens fans, 100 = most).   Lower means less obvious picks. - Variety in a top 10: average share of movie pairs in the list that have different genre sets   (1 minus genre Jaccard similarity, MovieLens genres). Models: popularity, item-kNN (top-100), RP3beta (top-100, shipped beta), and routed (what the app does). Rule written before running: these numbers describe the shipped models; nothing is tuned or changed because of them, and there's no pass or fail. Routed vs item-kNN gets paired-bootstrap 95% intervals on popularity of picks and variety (2,000 resamples of viewers). Coverage is reported as a single number. Writes data/beyond_accuracy.json.
